docs.title: Resource List
docs.text: Here is an updated, hopefully accurate, list of nearby locations to recycle. Please send any additions or corrections to me or Cattail.

docs.title: Mask
docs.text:
Recycling has a new mask for crushing glass! It's a GVS Elipse SPR549 Elipse Mask Integra P100, preventing cancer-causing silica from reaching your lungs. Check out its specifications and instructions for use. Since Cattail paid for it, it's your mask, too!

Note: these filters will not be effective against gases. Probably not the thing to take to a protest.

It is currently stored in a plastic bag inside of a banjo case with a "Rolling into Bloomfield" sticker on it. A more permanent home will most likely be found, but the important thing is to keep it out of dust.

The next step in improving the safety of the glass crusher is to get the shop-vac unit working (designed to draw away and trap glass dust), or to replace it. If anyone wants to help me with this, I imagine it would be creditable hours. If not, I would compensate you personally in exchange for my own edification and peace of mind.

docs.title: this website
docs.text:
I've told several people now how easy it is to make a website like this one. I still believe it to be true. It's free, and can be easily replicated. I could teach you how to do it in half an hour. Minimalist tech stack, open source.

Paying for anything, in my experience, means giving money away for the experience of being gaslit as to how necessary the tool you are paying for really is. Putting a target on your back to be marketed to, suckered into more subscriptions, taught how to interact with a black box, with skills that are not intended to be transferable.

docs.title: Metaphors
docs.text:
I've been thinking about how to repurpose, or recycle, my role as the village recyclist, to make it open source, adaptable, and modular.

One step will be to be more open and transparent about how I spend my recycling hours. Another will be to solicit ideas and feedback from the community.

Email me or Cattail with suggestions, or things to add to the below list.

docs.title: Respirator: GVS Elipse Integra P100 (SPR549)
docs.text: Community equipment — shared under Cattail Commons Co-op. Primary use: glass crushing/cullet processing. Also available to borrow for dust work (insulation, clay plaster mixing, sanding).

docs.title: Why this mask
docs.text: Glass crushing throws fine glass dust and silica particulate into the air — the kind of sub-micron particulate a basic dust mask doesn't stop. This model carries a P100 rating, NIOSH's highest particulate filter class, rated to capture ≥99.97% of particles at 0.3 microns. The "Integra" version adds a built-in goggle, so eye protection and respiratory protection share one seal — useful around a crusher where glass fragments and dust are both a hazard. Size is S/M.

docs.title: Specs
docs.text: Spec Detail Model GVS Elipse Integra P100, SPR549, S/M NIOSH approval P100, TC-84A-8119 (meets 42 CFR 84) Eye protection standard ANSI Z87+ Filter media HESPA (High Efficiency Synthetic Particulate Air), pleated, interchangeable Filtration efficiency ≥99.97% at 0.3 microns Breathing resistance ~3 mbar at 47.5 L/min per filter (increases as filter loads; max ~7 mbar before replacement needed) Lens Polycarbonate, anti-fog + anti-scratch coating Mask body Medical-grade TPE, latex- and silicone-free, odor-free Valve Nylon body, silicone diaphragm, large central non-return exhalation valve Strap 4-point adjustable elasticated head/neck strap Operating range -5°C to +55°C Replacement filter part # SPR321 (twin pack, fits S/M and M/L)

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
• Glass dust and cullet particulate from crushing operations
  • Silica dust, cement dust, stone/aggregate dust, wood dust, mold, and similar construction particulates (this is why it doubles for treehouse insulation/plaster/sanding work)
  • Situations needing simultaneous eye protection from flying fragments plus dust protection

docs.title: What it's NOT for
docs.text:
• Gases or vapors of any kind — this is a particulate-only (P100) filter. It will not protect against solvent fumes, paint vapors, ammonia, or other chemical vapors. (GVS sells separate OV/gas-cartridge Integra variants for that — this is not one of them.)
  • Oxygen-deficient atmospheres — not a substitute for supplied-air or SCBA equipment.
  • A compromised or unclear face seal — facial hair along the sealing surface, damaged straps, or a cracked mask body all break the seal and void the protection. Do not use if any of these apply.
  • Continuous/indefinite reuse of a single filter set — see replacement guidance below.
  • Anyone who hasn't checked the fit — S/M is one size; if it doesn't seal well on your face, it isn't providing rated protection regardless of the filter.

docs.title: Filter replacement
docs.text:
Replace filters when breathing becomes noticeably harder (a sign the filter is loading up with particulate) or if you can smell/taste contaminants through the mask (sign of a saturated filter or bad seal). Filtration efficiency stays constant at ~99.97% throughout the filter's usable life — it doesn't gradually leak more particulate, it just gets harder to breathe through until you swap it. Given glass-crushing dust load, expect this to be sooner rather than later — don't wait for a fixed calendar interval.

Order replacement filters (GVS SPR321, genuine, 2-pack): Amazon link

docs.title: Care & maintenance (shared/community equipment)
docs.text:
Since this is passed between users, hygiene matters more than it would for a personal respirator:

  1. After each use: wipe the mask body (not the filters) with a damp cloth and mild soap and water. Do not submerge the mask or filters in water — filters are water-resistant, not washable.
  2. Let it air dry completely before storing or handing off to the next person.
  3. Before each use: inspect the mask body, straps, and filters for cracks, damage, or wear. Don't use if the strap elastic is shot or the mask body is cracked.
  4. Storage: keep it in a clean, dry place away from direct sunlight and extreme temperatures — ideally sealed in a bag or container so the filters aren't picking up ambient dust between uses.

    Note: Currently in a banjo case on the shelf.

  5. If passing between different users regularly: consider keeping a small stock of spare filters on hand (see above) so a fresh filter can go in when hygiene or fit is a concern, rather than everyone sharing the same filter set indefinitely.
